about: The music player's order and fades (ADR 0135 decisions 6 and 7, ADR 0142 decision 1; ADR 0155 decision 7.2, the seventh slice). `randomInt`: the platform's unbiased draw in [0, n) from 32-bit words (the web's `crypto.getRandomValues` into a Uint32Array: a word is its four bytes little-endian), a word at or past the largest multiple of n below 2^32 drawn again; `expected` the value and how many words it took. `order`: a queue (`ids`, `startId`) under scripted randomness - `draws` lists every call in order as [n, value], and a client must ask exactly those n - then each `steps` op (`current`, `next`, `peek`, `previous` at `positionMs` into the track, `drop` an id, `size`) and its answer (`previous`: {restart: true} or {restart: false, id}; `drop`: null). `fades`: a span (`startMs`, `endMs`; an `endMs` of null is an unknown end, Infinity) and its fades in milliseconds of the file - an answer of null is Infinity - `fadeLengthAt` at each of `positionsMs`. Numbers are JavaScript's doubles.

randomInt.rule: a word below the limit: its remainder
the top word lies past the largest multiple of 3: drawn again
the last word below the limit of 3 is kept
a word whose bytes differ: read little-endian
n = 2^31 - 1, the largest a queue can be: the two top words are drawn again
n = 2^30 + 1: three quarters of the words are kept
n = 7, several rejections in a row
zero is a word like any other

order.rule: Fisher-Yates by the draws handed in: always 0
Fisher-Yates by the draws handed in: always n - 1 keeps the order
a round that would start with the track that ended the last one swaps it with a later one
the swap draws its partner among the rest of the round
2 tracks, 60 rounds: each a permutation, none starting with the last one played
3 tracks, 60 rounds: each a permutation, none starting with the last one played
4 tracks, 60 rounds: each a permutation, none starting with the last one played
5 tracks, 60 rounds: each a permutation, none starting with the last one played
seven tracks over three rounds
a start track plays first, the rest of its round shuffled
a start track the queue does not hold is no start track
a queue holds an id once, in its first place
a single track plays again and again, drawing nothing
an empty queue plays nothing
previous: more than 3 s in restarts, 3 s or less goes back, nothing before the first restarts, next goes forward again
peek fixes the next track without going there; next then goes to it
a dropped track leaves every round and the history; the queue empties when none is left
dropping a track played before keeps the one playing; an unknown id changes nothing
dropping the track playing goes back to the one before it
dropping a peeked track takes it out of the history ahead
after going back, a dropped track ahead is skipped going forward

fades.rule: a song fades out over 5 s at its trimmed end; a press over 1 s; a seek into the window shortens the fade
a track shorter than two fades fades over a third of its span
a third of a span that does not divide by three is not rounded
a tiny track: a press no longer than its own fade
exactly two fades long: the whole 5 s
just under two fades: a third
a press over a span of 3 s less a millisecond is a third of it
fractional edges, as a file's duration in seconds times 1000 gives them
an unknown end: the whole fade, never reached
an unknown end after a leading silence
an empty span fades over nothing
